Criterion 2.5
Benthic Impact
How do I interpret this requirement?
o
The method for benthic monitoring for cage culture and suspended marine mollusc systems
is composed of:
Sediment sampling zones and sampling locations across transects.
Benthic quality categories and thresholds for defining those categories and the benthic
status.
Sampling approach
o
The method uses a three-level sampling approach:
The number of transects and sampling locations, as well as the complexity of analysis, may
increase based on Level 1 or Level 2 monitoring results:

Level  1  requires  sampling  along  one  transect  in  the  direction  of  the  predominant
current. The samples are to be analysed for redox potential and total free sulphide.
Direction of the predominant current is the compass direction in which the water
flows the majority of the time.
Level  2  requires  sampling  along  three  additional  transects.  The  samples  are  to  be
analysed for redox potential and total free sulphide.
Level 3 requires sampling as per Level 2 (at a minimum, on the two transects in the
direction of the predominant current). The samples are to be analysed for three (of the
14) biotic indicators selected from Table 2 of Appendix 7 (7.1).
Sites  should  select  biotic  indicators  that  are  more  appropriate  based  on  their
location or based on regulatory requirements.
o
In Scotland, sites should select AZTI's Marine Biotic Index (AMBI) as one of the
biotic  indicators  since  it  is  a  component  of  the  Infaunal  Quality  Index  (IQI)
required by the regulation in that country.
Sites can choose to commence monitoring at any of the three levels.
Previous  benthic  impact  results  can  provide  an  indication  of  the  level  at  which
monitoring should commence.
The same sediment samples collected for Level 1 or Level 2 sampling can be used for the
analysis required by Level 3 sampling.
Sites are not required to collect new sediment samples.
Transects:
In cases where a transect overlaps with another site, the direction of the overlapping
transect should be adjusted.
The same applies to any transect/sampling station overlapping with land.
Transect directions should also be adjusted to avoid sampling in areas where water
depth changes rapidly along the transect.
In all cases, each transect should be as close to 90 degrees from each other as possible.
In cases where multiple cages are located in close proximity, transects should be
located at the edge of the last cage site.
Given the low complexity associated with Level 1 and Level 2 sampling and analysis, it is
advisable for sites to conduct monitoring not only at the required timings by the indicator
but also prior to those timings

The results can indicate the need for Level 3 sampling at the timings required by the

Ecological Quality Status (EQS) categories
o
Ecological Quality Status (EQS) categories are used to determine the benthic status (see more
details on the categories in the Useful Resources section).
Compliance Framework
o
A numerical scoring method that combines all indicator data collected from each sampling
zone is used to determine the EQS Category and benthic status:
The method requires calculating the mean value for each indicator in each sampling zone
to determine the Indicator EQS Score for that zone.
Next, an overall Zone EQS Score is calculated by combining the Indicator EQS Scores.
The overall Zone EQS Score is used to determine the final EQS Category for each sampling
zone and the 'acceptable' benthic status.
In the case of cages, the EQS Category of the Reference Zone will determine the EQS
Categories for 'acceptable' benthic status of the sampling zones.
Sampling Timing
o
Sampling is required to be conducted during the period when the benthic impact is expected
to be highest, i.e. at peak impact, and uses proxies for determining peak impact:
Peak biomass (cage culture and suspended marine mollusc systems).
Maximum annual bottom water temperature (cage culture and suspended marine
mollusc systems).
Peak feeding (cage culture only).
By considering these proxies, cage culture sites shall (see Appendix 7 (7.2.1 and 7.3.1)):
Provide the CAB with information on when the highest impact on the benthos is
predicted to occur.
Determine the timing sampling that applies.
o

and for suspended marine mollusc systems, the requirements allow for
